_comment_modes: Each mode is a client EXE plus the .csgalaxy pass file handed to it as its
single command-line argument — which is all a drag-and-drop ever did.
There are three EXEs today only because the localhost redirect and the
code patches that TestBed needs have not been reconciled into one binary.
When they are, this file is the only thing that changes: point every mode
at the same 'exe' and delete the others from build.ps1's copy list.
SINGLE PLAYER USES Resurgence.exe, NOT TestBed.exe, and the difference is
not cosmetic. Launched on a .dat, TestBed.exe loads the save correctly and
then never resolves a turn -- the counter does not move however short the
turn length is set. Resurgence.exe on the same .dat advances normally.
Measured both ways against the same file. Neither contacts the server on
the .dat path, so the client's flashing 'disconnected' indicator is
expected there and is not the cause.
needs_server  documentation, not control flow — the launcher always runs
the stub server. Measured, not assumed: Tutorial calls
localhost:8888 at startup, Demo never contacts it at all.
show          false keeps a mode out of the player-facing window without
losing the mapping.
enabled       false renders the card greyed out with a COMING SOON badge.
Such a mode needs no exe or galaxy, and is skipped when
looking for the game files.
ai            the opponent. The heuristic AI is a separate process that
plays a civ by reading and writing the running client's
memory, so it is started after the game and killed with it.
'civ' MUST match the name the engine gives the rival civ in
that galaxy — measured, not assumed: the human is
'DemoPlayer' (from the .csgalaxy pass token) and the rival
is 'BadGuy'. A mode with no 'ai' key simply has no opponent.
